text:
Predicates:
Reads(x, y) ::: x reads y.
GainsKnowledge(x) ::: x gains knowledge.
Smarter(x) ::: x becomes smarter.
Book(y) ::: y is a book.
Author(y, z) ::: y is authored by z.
Title(y, t) ::: y has title t.
Person(x) ::: x is a person.
Premises:
Books contain knowledge. ::: (No formal predicate needed)
∀x ∀y (Reads(x, y) → GainsKnowledge(x)) ::: When a person reads a book, that person gains knowledge.
∀x (GainsKnowledge(x) → Smarter(x)) ::: If a person gains knowledge, they become smarter.
Harry read the book “Walden” by Henry Thoreau. ::: ∃y (Book(y) ∧ Author(y, HenryThoreau) ∧ Title(y, “Walden”) ∧ Reads(Harry, y))
Conclusion:
Harry is smarter than before. ::: Smarter(Harry)
